display.purpose: Hero name only. Space Grotesk 500, clamp to 3.75rem.

headline.purpose: Section titles; open with a mono tagline beneath.

label.purpose: Terminal eyebrow labels, uppercase mono 11px, 0.18em tracking.

mono.purpose: All data, commands, chips, nav links, form values.

shadows.name: panel-top-highlight
shadows.purpose: The single sanctioned shadow: an inset top highlight on console panels that reads as edge-lit machined metal. No ambient shadows exist.

motion.name: boot-type-in
motion.purpose: The hero boot console types its system report line by line at 240ms per line.

motion.name: cursor-blink
motion.purpose: The blinking amber block cursor (▊) at the boot-console insertion point.

motion.name: pulse-dot
motion.purpose: Pulsing status lamp on navbar mark, footer, and online indicators (ring expands to 6px fade).

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Phosphor-amber filled CTA for the primary action (view experience, send message, open a channel).

components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 44px; padding: 0 16px; border: none; border-radius: 0.5rem; background: #f5b04c; color: #1a1205; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 400; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary .ds-icon { width: 16px; height: 16px; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: rgba(245,176,76,0.9); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #0b0d10, 0 0 0 4px #f5b04c; }

components.name: Outline Button

components.name: Text Input

components.name: Console Panel

components.css: .ds-nav { position: sticky; top: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; height: 64px; padding: 0 24px; border-bottom: 1px solid #23292f; background: rgba(11,13,16,0.9); backdrop-filter: blur(8px); } .ds-nav-mark { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 14px; color: #e7e9ec; text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav-prompt { color: #f5b04c; } .ds-status-dot { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #f5b04c; box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 rgba(245,176,76,0.5); animation: ds-pulse 2.2s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-nav-links { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; } .ds-nav-links a { padding: 8px 12px; border-radius: 0.5rem; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 13px; color: #c7cdd4; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease; } .ds-nav-links a:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.05); color: #e7e9ec; } .ds-nav-links .ds-nav-cta { margin-left: 8px; background: #f5b04c; color: #1a1205; } .ds-nav-links .ds-nav-cta:hover { background: rgba(245,176,76,0.9); color: #1a1205; } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 rgba(245,176,76,0.5); } 50% { opacity: 0.6; box-shadow: 0 0 0 6px rgba(245,176,76,0); } }

components.css: .ds-term { border: 1px solid #23292f; border-radius: 0.6rem; overflow: hidden; background: #111418; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.03) inset; } .ds-term-head { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; padding: 12px 16px; border-bottom: 1px solid #23292f; background: #0e1115; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 12px; color: #6c757f; } .ds-term-dots { display: flex; gap: 6px; } .ds-term-dots span { width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #3a444f; } .ds-term-body { min-height: 300px; padding: 20px; background: #0a0c0e; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.6; } .ds-term-body pre { margin: 0; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #e7e9ec; } .ds-cmd { color: #e7e9ec; } .ds-out { color: #9fb4a8; } .ds-read { color: #5bc3e0; } .ds-ok { color: #4caf7d; } .ds-cursor { display: inline-block; color: #f5b04c; animation: ds-blink 1.1s steps(2, start) infinite; } @keyframes ds-blink { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0; } }

narrative.overview: Hayti's portfolio presents itself as a live status console for a service called `hayti.kafley` — a developer-tool, SRE-flavored surface where reliability, observability, and backend depth are the interface itself rather than decoration. The site refuses the generic dark-hero-portfolio template that leads with identical icon cards; it leads instead with a boot console that types a system self-report onto dark glass: whoami, --focus, systemctl status, uptime, signal --observability.
keyCharacteristics: Carbon-black ground with a faint 44px engineering grid; no photo, no imagery — the console is the identity.
Graphite panels with hairline borders carry every record; depth comes from tonal layering, not shadows.
One phosphor-amber signal color owns all interactivity, focus, and status lamp; cyan and green are stage readings only.
JetBrains Mono for all data/labels/chips; Space Grotesk only for display titles.
One authored moment of motion: the hero boot-console type-in with a blinking block cursor and a pulsing status dot.

rules.name: The Single Console Voice Rule
rules.body: Phosphor amber is the only color that carries chrome and interactivity — CTAs, prompts, focus, status lamps. Cyan and green appear exclusively as stage readings and status conditions (--observability output, status: online); neither may ever be used as a button fill, border, or navigational device.

rules.name: The Rarity Discipline
rules.body: Saturated color covers a small fraction of any screen. The ground is graphite; amber is earned in specific, repeated places (the CTA, the prompt mark, the status lamp), never strewn as decoration.

rules.name: The Mono-For-Data Rule
rules.body: Any datum, label, chip, or command is set in JetBrains Mono. Space Grotesk is reserved for display titles and a handful of human headings; a phrase read like telemetry must be mono.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat and separated by 1px hairlines of Hairline (#23292f) — borders, divide-y rows, section rules. There are no ambient shadows. To make a panel feel dimensional, use a tonal step up or the single inset top highlight, never a drop shadow.

dos: Do lead with the console — every new screen should read as a pane of a monitored system, not a marketing page.
Do give each record a Hairline-bordered console-panel container with a well-colored header and mono metadata.
Do spend phosphor amber only on interactive chrome, focus, and status lamps; reserve cyan and green for stage readings and status.
Do set every datum, label, chip, and command in JetBrains Mono; Space Grotesk is for display titles only.
Do keep surfaces flat and separate them with 1px hairlines and tonal steps; the single sanctioned shadow is the inset top highlight (0 1px 0 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.03)).
Do keep motion to the boot console's type-in, blinking cursor, and pulsing status dot — no entrance animations, no shimmer.
Do use the console-panel, console-grid, term-label, status-dot, and section-title composite classes for consistency.
donts: Don't use cyan or green as a button fill, border, or navigation device — readouts never become chrome.
Don't introduce drop shadows or lifted/card-hover elevation; depth is tonal and hairline only.
Don't add the generic dark-hero-portfolio pattern — identical icon cards, ambient gradients, or a photo hero. The console is the hero.
Don't animate page entry, scroll reveals, or hover lift; only the boot console types, the cursor blinks, and the status dot pulses.
Don't put body copy in mono or headings in the system font; respect the fixed machine/human split.
Don't restate a color in prose with a different value than its frontmatter hex — the frontmatter is normative.
